key_insight: DSGNAR is a scalable second-order optimizer that tackles the core PINN bottleneck—ill-conditioned training—to deliver far higher accuracy and faster convergence than prior methods.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more practical for high-accuracy PDE solving in scientific and engineering workflows, especially where classical solver-like precision is needed.
method: Doubly-sketched Gauss-Newton approximation for scalable second-order updates
Adaptive ratio strategy to control regularization and step length
Designed to be robust across precision, architectures, and hyperparameters
evidence_signal: Across nonlinear, chaotic, multi-scale, high-dimensional, and Navier-Stokes benchmarks, the method achieved errors as low as 3×10^-16 in double precision, improved Burgers' results by five orders of magnitude, and reached 4.75×10^-7 in single precision in under ten seconds.
watch_item: Second-order sketched methods can still be sensitive to implementation details, memory/compute overhead, and the quality of sketching on very large or stiff PDE systems.
paper_title: An Optimisation Framework for the Well-Conditioned Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
